question: A 62-year-old man comes to the physician for evaluation of an increasing right-sided cheek swelling for 2 years. He has had recurrent right-sided oral ulcers for the past 2 months. He has smoked a pack of cigarettes daily for 30 years. He drinks a beer every night. His temperature is 37.1°C (98.8°F), pulse is 71/min, respirations are 14/min, and blood pressure is 129/83 mm Hg. Examination shows a mild, nontender swelling above the angle of the right jaw. There is no overlying erythema or induration. There are multiple shallow ulcers on the right buccal mucosa and mandibular marginal gingiva. There is no lymphadenopathy. Ultrasound shows a soft tissue mass in the parotid gland. An ultrasound-guided biopsy of the mass confirms the diagnosis of parotid adenoid cystic carcinoma. A right-sided total parotidectomy is scheduled. This patient is at greatest risk for which of the following early complications?

options.opa: Hyperesthesia of the right ear lobe
options.opd: Paralysis of the right lower lip
options.ope: Impaired taste and sensation of the posterior 1/3 of the tongue

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Smoking -> increased risk of developing parotid adenoid cystic carcinoma -> 80% CHAIN: Parotid adenoid cystic carcinoma -> total parotidectomy -> risk of early complications -> 70% CHAIN: Total parotidectomy -> potential damage to the facial nerve -> risk of paralysis of the right lower lip -> 80%
analysis: Given the diagnosis of parotid adenoid cystic carcinoma and the planned right-sided total parotidectomy, the patient is at greatest risk for damage to the facial nerve during surgery, which could result in paralysis of the right lower lip.
